did_you_know.text: Did you know? Chapter 12 opens with a summary of Israel’s conquests east of the Jordan, from the Arnon Valley to Mount Hermon and throughout the Arabah east of the Jordan.

Did you know? Sihon king of the Amorites is described as ruling from Heshbon over territory stretching from the Arnon Valley to the Jabbok Valley, with the Jabbok serving as the border of the Ammonites.
Did you know? Sihon’s territory is described as including the Arabah as far as the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, as well as the area below the slopes of Pisgah.
Did you know? Og king of Bashan is described as living in Ashtaroth and Edrei and ruling over Mount Hermon, Salecah, and all Bashan as far as the borders of the Geshurites and Maacathites.
Did you know? According to the chapter, Moses and the Israelites defeated Sihon and Og, and Moses gave their land as an inheritance to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

Did you know? After summarizing the conquests east of the Jordan, the chapter turns to Joshua’s conquests west of the Jordan; Joshua gave the land to the tribes of Israel according to their divisions.

Did you know? The land west of the Jordan is described in the chapter as consisting of several regions—the hill country, the foothills, the Arabah, the slopes, the wilderness, and the Negev—and six peoples who had previously lived there are also listed.
Did you know? The list of the kings of Canaan begins with the king of Jericho and the king of Ai, naming one king for each of these cities.
Did you know? At the end of the list, the chapter states that Joshua and the Israelites defeated a total of thirty-one kings.
